passages.provision_quote: Any sentence enhancement that was imposed prior to January 1, 2018, pursuant to Section 11370.2 of the Health and Safety Code, except for any enhancement imposed for a prior conviction of violating or conspiring to violate Section 11380 of the Health and Safety Code is legally invalid.
passages.note: Allen-authored bill that voids two prior sentence enhancements and orders resentencing to a lesser sentence; it lowers punishment but names no treatment, service or restitution.
passages.actor_quote: SB 483, Allen. Sentencing: resentencing to remove sentencing enhancements.

rows.reasoning: Allen authored SB 483 (2021-2022), which declares the prior-prison-term and controlled-substance sentence enhancements "legally invalid" and requires courts to recall and resentence so that resentencing "shall result in a lesser sentence than the one originally imposed". Removing enhancements reduces punishment, but the bill supplies no "support and treatment" and no chance to "make things right through service or restitution", and it states no case-by-case orientation, so it establishes a side of the ladder rather than any rung's clauses.
